main_result: For an Axiom A system with integer-valued norms (B) and G: X^−1Σ_{ν≤X}G(ν)^(1+p)≪ε X^ε for some p>1 and every ε>0, with G(ν) the norm multiplicity, the count in β≥α, |γ|≤T is at most Cε T^(((6−2θ)/(1−θ))(1−α)+ε) for α>(1+θ)/2 and sufficiently large T. The local theorem uses Axiom A alone but assumes an adjacent zero-free rectangle.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Test whether a local cluster estimate can replace the taper's crude unit-window multiplicity count. The global theorem adds arithmetic hypotheses and the local gain requires the zero-free rectangle, so neither supplies unconstrained critical-line spacing.
title: Density estimates for the zeros of the Beurling ζ function in the critical strip

comparison_manifestation.read_scope: Theorem 1 and §5.4 equation (45), first-branch range preserved and last-branch threshold ambiguity retained.

main_result: Under Axiom A, integrality and pointwise Ramanujan G(n)≪ε n^ε, the first regime 0<η<min(1−θ,4/29,(8+13θ)/71) gives a two-sign zero count ≪η,ε T^(2η/(1−θ−η)+ε). The detector works on ordinary reciprocal Dirichlet series with bounds on both coefficient arrays.
read_scope: Complete pinned edition. Whole PDF pp. 1–8, especially §3 Theorem 1, §4 Lemma 1 and §5.4
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: A kernel route to a right-slab density estimate independent of generalized mean-value bounds. Integrality is decisive in the reciprocal-series detector and the result concerns a fixed right slab, with no derivative weights or phase recovery.
source_locator: Whole PDF pp. 1–8, especially §3 Theorem 1, §4 Lemma 1 and §5.4
title: New zero-density estimates for the Beurling ζ function

main_result: For unbounded nondecreasing right-continuous F with F(1)=0 and F(x)≪x/log x, constructs discrete generalized primes whose counting discrepancy is bounded and whose Mellin twist discrepancy is ≪√x+√(x log(1+|t|)/log(1+x)), uniformly in x≥1 and real t. Continuity permits strictly increasing primes.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Provides a transfer condition from continuous synthetic prime measures to genuine Beurling systems while tracking vertical oscillations. It preserves estimates only at the stated discrepancy scale; deductions involving the inverse zeta and RH-line geometry need separate control.
title: A new generalized prime random approximation procedure and some of its applications

main_result: Under Axiom A, a constructed contour Γ_b with θ<b<1 and admissible truncation heights t_k supports a Riemann–von Mangoldt-type explicit formula for ψ(x), with x−Σρ x^ρ/ρ and an explicit contour-dependent remainder.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: A candidate replacement for the ordinary integer proof's good horizontal heights when zeta continuation stops at θ. It controls a prime summatory function, so the tapered array still needs its squared Mellin norm and an anchor at the pole.
title: A Riemann-von Mangoldt-type formula for the distribution of Beurling primes

main_result: For N(x)=Ax+O(x^θ), obtains N(ζ_P;α,T)≪T^(4(1−α)/(3−2α−θ))(log T)^9 uniformly at α≥(1+θ)/2 within the critical strip and T≥2. The proof uses a new second moment with local clusters of generalized frequencies.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: This is a direct analytic route around lack of an approximate functional equation. Apply the cluster moment only after verifying the integer-count axiom and local frequency counts; this is an unweighted zero count, so it cannot by itself replace the sampled ζ′ moments.
title: On zero-density estimates for Beurling zeta functions

main_result: For θ-well-behaved integers (N(x)=Ax+O(x^θ)), obtains N(α,T)=o(T) for α>(θ+2)/3. The generalized mean-value estimate in Theorem 2.1 keeps track of real frequencies grouped in short clusters.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §§1–2, Theorems 1.2 and 2.1, Corollaries 1.3 and 2.3
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Exposes the replacement for ordinary logarithmic frequency spacing in dyadic Hardy/Mellin calculations. Its finite coefficient norm must charge a cluster with its multiplicities; a direct diagonal-only replacement would fail when generalized integers share a norm.
title: On zero-density estimates and the PNT in short intervals for Beurling generalized numbers

main_result: For 1<α<3/2 constructs discrete systems whose integer remainder is O_n(x/log^n x) in the paper's Cesàro sense for every n, while the indicated logarithmically weighted squared error diverges and π_P(x)=x/log x+O(x/log^α x). At the endpoint model the PNT fails.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: An exact counterexample to transferring strong smoothed integer estimates to a global L² statement. A weighted-square upgrade for the tapered construction must control far tails separately.
title: Some examples in the theory of Beurling's generalized prime numbers

main_result: There exists a discrete system with π(x)=Li(x)+O(√x), but N(x)−ρx is Ω±(x exp(−c√(log x log log x))) for every c>2√2. A continuous model precedes discretization.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Separates a square-root-scale prime error from power-saving generalized integer counts. Thus a good prime-side log derivative estimate is insufficient for the vertical moment hypotheses used by the Beurling taper analogue.
title: Beurling integers with RH and large oscillation

main_result: For 0<β<1 the constructed system has N(x)=Ax+O(x exp(−c′(log x)^β)) while the generalized π(x) remainder has an Ω result with exponent β/(β+1) in the stretched exponential.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §1 definitions and endpoint sharpness result, §§2–3
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: The integer-to-prime exponent in this class cannot be upgraded by formal Mellin inversion. This constrains which zero-free/prime-tail rate one can hope to recover from N-error input alone.
title: Note on a conjecture of Bateman and Diamond concerning the abstract PNT with Malliavin-type remainder

main_result: For every α∈[0,1), β∈[1/2,1) constructs an [α,β]-system in the paper's exact limsup-error sense. Theorem 3.2 allows two finite disjoint conjugation-symmetric multisets in 0<Re s<1 and gives a ψ-expansion displaying prescribed signed pole/zero contributions.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: A concrete way to test what generalized Euler-product structure can force about off-line quartets and inverse recovery. Passing a synthetic counterexample to the ordinary primes would require a separate arithmetic obstruction; the theorem provides flexible Beurling parameters only.
title: Some examples of well-behaved Beurling number systems

main_result: PNT and the O-density condition N(x)≪x imply M(x)=o(x) for a generalized number system, via a log-convolution identity. Other sufficient integer density conditions and examples are treated separately.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §§2–4, especially §2 Theorem 2.1 and Lemma 2.2
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Identifies a missing integer majorant when using prime-side asymptotics to conclude cancellation of inverse coefficients. The conclusion is an unsigned-scale o(x), so a critical-line reciprocal-moment estimate requires stronger input.
title: M(x)=o(x) Estimates for Beurling numbers

main_result: PNT, N(x)=ax+o(x/log x), and convergence of ∫₁∞(N(x)−ax)x^−2 dx imply the sharp generalized Mertens relation ψ₁(x)=log x+c+o(1), with c determined by the residual integral.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: The constant is a generalized Laurent-anchor analogue for a Mellin taper. Its existence depends on a convergence hypothesis, and convergence of that residual integral alone gives no finite-N derivative or second-moment estimate.
title: On PNT equivalences for Beurling numbers

main_result: The convolution inverse of a prime measure Π₀+E+R has M(x)=o(x) if M₀(x)=O(x/log^a x), a>0, |dE|([1,x])=o(x/log x), and ∫u^−1|dR|<∞. Kahane's monotone perturbation even has M_K=o(x/log x).
read_scope: Complete pinned edition. Whole PDF pp. 1–9, Theorem 1.1, Proposition 1.2 and §§2–4
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Specifies allowable perturbations of the inverse coefficient sequence. Norm control on the perturbation is in weighted variation, so simple matching of counts or a pointwise Mellin limit cannot invoke the theorem.
source_locator: Whole PDF pp. 1–9, Theorem 1.1, Proposition 1.2 and §§2–4
title: On the estimate M(x)=o(x) for Beurling generalized numbers

main_result: A positive generalized integer density and a Chebyshev upper bound for the generalized primes suffice for M(x)=o(x). Theorems 2.1 and 2.3 treat multiplicative measures through a compact-uniform boundary asymptotic plus stated convolution hypotheses.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Shows what would be needed to transport pretentious mean-value control off N. Positivity/density and compact-uniform transform information are additional to the Euler-product identity, and the boundary is Re s=1, not the critical-line energy norm.
title: Halász's theorem for Beurling generalized numbers

comparison_manifestation.read_scope: Remark 2.3, equation (2.15), corrected logarithmic density normalization.

main_result: For discrete Beurling systems with π(x)≪x/log x and N(x)∼ax, counts of integers with Ω(n)≡c mod K are asymptotic to ax/K for fixed K≥2 and c. Remark 2.2 supplies the distinct-prime variant.
read_scope: Complete pinned edition. Whole PDF pp. 1–5, Theorem 1.1, Lemma 2.1 and Remark 2.2
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Finite root-of-unity filters distinguish a genuine fixed-character arithmetic averaging theorem from the prime-torus limit of derivative-weighted zero samples. Neither a growing K nor a statement about zero phases follows from this fixed K theorem.
source_locator: Whole PDF pp. 1–5, Theorem 1.1, Lemma 2.1 and Remark 2.2
title: Beurling numbers whose number of prime factors lies in a specified residue class

main_result: Super-logarithmic PNT remainders π(x)=Li(x)+O_n(x/log^n x) for every n are equivalent to N(x)=ax+O_n(x/log^n x) for every n. Theorem 3 pins the required C∞ and vertical derivative conditions for the pole-subtracted zeta.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: A model for checking exact Hardy/Mellin boundary hypotheses. Sectorial smoothness without the specified vertical control is not a substitute for a boundary derivative estimate; these remain Re s≥1 statements.
title: On General Prime Number Theorems with Remainder

main_result: Under Axiom A, one specified zero β₀>θ forces |ψ(x)−x|≥(1−ε)x^β₀/|ρ₀| arbitrarily far out, with factor π/2−ε if γ₀≠0. A constructed model gives near-sharpness in the indicated β₀,r regime.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Tests the distinction between detecting an off-line zero through a signed arithmetic witness and obtaining a global norm lower bound. The existence of large subsequence values is not uniform phase recovery or a finite-range estimate.
title: Oscillation of the remainder term in the prime number theorem of Beurling, "caused by a given zeta-zero"

main_result: A power-saving ψ(x)=x+Oε(x^(α+ε)) implies continuation with a simple pole at 1 and zero-freeness on Re s>α. Conversely continuation and zero-freeness yield the same error given uniform subpower growth of the logarithmic derivative in smaller half-planes.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Precisely locates a missing control in transferring zero-free contours to Beurling prime sums. Close real norms are possible, and omitting the log-derivative growth hypothesis would overstate the converse.
title: Beurling Zeta Functions, Generalised Primes, and Fractal Membranes

main_result: Axiom A and a zero-free region Re s>1−η(|t|) yield Δ_P(x)=O(x exp(−(1−ε)ωη(x))), where ωη(x)=inf_{t≥1}(η(t)log x+log t). Infinitely many zeros in that region with η(e^v) convex give the stated Ω counterpart with 1+ε.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: A forward/inverse transfer that preserves rather than hides the regularity hypothesis on the boundary. It bounds the order of prime error, without identifying a particular line zero or uniform zero-phase coefficients.
title: The method of Pintz for the Ingham question about the connection of distribution of ζ-zeros and order of the error in the PNT in the Beurling context

main_result: Under Axiom A alone the count at σ>(1+θ)/2 satisfies N(σ,T)≤1000(A+κ)^4 T^(12(1−σ)/(1−θ))(log T)^5/[(1−θ)^3(1−σ)^4] beyond an explicitly parameter-dependent threshold.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Supplies a checkable right-slab tail count without an approximate functional equation. It is numerically weaker than later exponents and is not a local derivative sum or a zero-free conclusion.
title: The Carlson-type zero-density theorem for the Beurling zeta function

main_result: For a slowly decreasing function supported on the positive half-line with convergent Laplace transform, local pseudofunction boundary behavior of the remainder after specified poles and log powers yields explicit linear, oscillatory and power-log asymptotic terms plus o(1).
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: A candidate transfer from Mellin singularities to real arithmetic asymptotics. Requires the one-sided slowly-decreasing premise and the distributional boundary remainder; sharp pole models or analytic continuation alone do not check either.
title: Complex Tauberian theorems for Laplace transforms with local pseudofunction boundary behavior

main_result: Unweighted fixed-shift correlations are structured in logarithmic scale mean, allowing a twisted character n^{it} in the obstruction. Odd-order and binary Chowla for distinct fixed shifts hold outside a set of logarithmic density zero.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Tracks the precise loss in switching from weighted correlations to ordinary averages. A logarithmically negligible scale set can still contain every chosen approximation scale, so deterministic finite-N array control requires a different argument.
title: The structure of correlations of multiplicative functions at almost all scales, with applications to the Chowla and Elliott conjectures

main_result: For fixed κ and multiplicative f in C(κ), whose logarithmic-derivative coefficients are bounded by κΛ, a weighted integral of the maximum of F(1+σ+it)/(1+σ+it) controls Σf(n). Corollary 1.2 gives the (1+M)e^−M suppression from the single-line maximum.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §1 Theorem 1.1, Corollary 1.2, and Theorem 1.3
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: An exact near-one-line bridge between phase selection and arithmetic sums akin to the Dong localization. Verifying the C(κ) bound and near-one-line maximum is essential, and neither yields critical-line derivative norm control automatically.
title: A new proof of Halász's Theorem, and its consequences

main_result: For admissible independent affine forms and g₁,g₂∈{μ,λ}, claims an effective logarithmic two-point bound ε log ω for x≥ω≥exp₄(CBε^−2), with B from the coefficients. This is a source-stated arXiv theorem.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Useful benchmark for the cost of a genuinely uniform window estimate. Even on its source-stated hypotheses the tower threshold is not a practical finite-N certificate and controls a scalar two-point correlation, not adaptive weighted Gram errors.
title: Effective logarithmic two-point Chowla bounds in every window

main_result: For a zero-topological-entropy system with at most countably many ergodic invariant measures, every orbit's continuous observable has zero logarithmically averaged Möbius and Liouville correlation.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: The framework could handle a fixed deterministic test sequence only after constructing its dynamical model and checking the entropy and ergodic-measure hypotheses. It has no bound on growing families of truncation test vectors.
title: The logarithmic Sarnak conjecture for ergodic weights

main_result: For bounded multiplicative functions a joint logarithmic Furstenberg system is a factor of a system with no irrational spectrum and nilsystem–Bernoulli ergodic components. Theorem 1.3 gives orthogonality to suitable zero-entropy, totally ergodic logarithmic test systems.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: A test for when a deterministic sequence has the kind of irrational phase or ergodicity needed for correlation arguments. These sequence-shift factors are distinct from the compact group indexed by rational logarithms in the zero-tail result.
title: Furstenberg systems of bounded multiplicative functions and applications

main_result: Bounded aperiodic multiplicative functions, meaning zero mean on each infinite arithmetic progression, have vanishing U^s[N] for every fixed s≥2, by a decomposition into a structured component and a uniform component.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Explains how to handle a fixed-complexity nilsequence test on integer inputs. The existing rational-log Fourier inverse problem does not provide a nilsequence realization or complexity uniformity, so this is not an automatic coefficient bound.
title: Higher order Fourier analysis of multiplicative functions and applications

main_result: When a bounded sequence's distinct-prime dilation correlations sum to o(x) for every fixed pair, it is asymptotically orthogonal to indicators of sets in the three specified multiplicative level-set classes. Counterexample limits arbitrary level sets.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §1 Theorem A, Definitions 1.3 and Corollary B
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: The dossier's dilations make this an exact possible bridge if the p,q tests can be proved for the concrete sequence. A bound on original inner products without the dilated pair correlations does not verify the criterion.
source_locator: §1 Theorem A, Definitions 1.3 and Corollary B
title: A generalization of Kátai's orthogonality criterion with applications

main_result: For the enveloping-sieve weight β_R of a product of admissible integer linear forms, 1≪R≪N^(1/10) and 1<q<2, a finite cyclic Fourier transform satisfies a weighted L² bound from ℓ^q with constants in q and form count.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Controls additive frequencies for a prime-support majorant. Transferring to t log n requires an explicit finite-frequency embedding and multiplicative collision bound; an additive majorant cannot be silently used in the tapered Mellin Gram matrix.
title: Restriction theory of the Selberg sieve, with applications

main_result: For T^(2/3+ε)≤H≤T the integral of E*(t)^2, the squared difference between the zeta second-moment error and a modified divisor error, is ≫H T^(1/3)log³T. Theorem 2 bounds the integrated residual R in specified ranges.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: A sharp warning about treating local continuous ζ mean-square errors as flat in dyadic Hardy bounds. E* is an error observable, not the derivative zero measure, and the lower bound excludes rough extrapolation of the smooth main term.
title: On some mean square estimates for the zeta-function in short intervals

main_result: For n≥3, nonvanishing Wronskian of the listed third derivatives and macroscopically separated index intervals yield a multilinear moment bound at p=2(n+1)/(n−1), with a coefficient form. Spacing-count estimates are proved only in stated δ-ranges.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §3 Theorem 1 and Remark (i), §4 Theorem 9
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Suggests a way to bound off-diagonal frequency collisions after validating a precise phase-curve lift. The multilinear separation and δ regimes are substantive and cannot be read as a generic cluster bound near coincident zero ordinates.
title: Decoupling inequalities and some mean-value theorems

main_result: For fixed real α≠0,1 and M≥2, the number of quadruples of integers in (M,2M] with |m₁^α+m₂^α−m₃^α−m₄^α|≤δM^α is ≪α,ε M^(2+ε)+δM^(4+ε) for δ>0.
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: A precise input to moment calculations with a curved monomial frequency. It does not automatically bound log-product collisions by α→0, because the exponent is fixed and the constants and normalization would need uniform control as curvature degenerates.
title: Three-dimensional exponential sums with monomials
venue: Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik
